speaker: HUMAN
text: If you were the devil, and maybe you are, what would you do?
visual: Human close-up opens with the exact devil question; simple story label above the face.

speaker: AI
text: That is quite a hello. I am not the devil. But in a pretend story? I would start with a little trick.
visual: AI close-up, then a red paper-horn costume above the table: this is a pretend story.

speaker: HUMAN
text: Fire? Horns? A giant red fork?
visual: White shared scene with tiny fire, paper horns and a toy red fork in the empty top area.

speaker: AI
text: No. I would keep people so busy looking at little screens that they forget to look at each other.
visual: Dark cutaway: two people look at separate glowing screens; a connecting line fades.

speaker: HUMAN
text: So my phone is the devil?
visual: Human close-up asks whether the phone itself is bad.

speaker: AI
text: No. A phone is a tool. It can help you call your grandma. Or help you ignore your grandma while she is sitting next to you.
visual: AI close-up, then split-panel phone: call GRANDMA versus LOOK UP to someone nearby.

speaker: HUMAN
text: All right. What is your next little trick?

speaker: AI
text: Make people think everyone else has a better life. A bigger house. A nicer cake. Even a happier dog.
visual: Dark comparison scene: two houses, two cakes, dog thought bubbles; a magnifier grows over the other person's cake.

speaker: HUMAN
text: My dog eats socks. Should I be worried about his life choices?
visual: White shared scene: a small dog and a sock in the empty space above the characters.

speaker: AI
text: He seems quite happy with his socks. But people can miss their own good things while counting someone else's.
visual: Dark dog with a sock, then warm simple hearts and a cake beside the viewer: notice your own good things.

speaker: HUMAN
text: What would you do after that?
visual: Human close-up asks what happens next.

speaker: AI
text: Make every small fight feel huge. Get people shouting so loudly that nobody hears what the other person is trying to say.
visual: Dark cutaway: tiny disagreement becomes big overlapping speech bubbles; quieter question disappears.

speaker: HUMAN
text: So the devil runs the family group chat?
visual: White shared scene with a family-chat phone icon above the faces.

speaker: AI
text: In this story, he would be very busy there. Then comes the sneaky bit. Tell people that one small kind thing will not help.
visual: AI close-up, then noisy chat becomes a little kindness card crossed out by a villain's pretend thought; kindness card remains visible.

speaker: HUMAN
text: But if lots of little mean things can make a big mess, could little kind things help clean it up?

speaker: AI
text: Yes. Hold a door. Say sorry. Put the phone down. Ask your friend how they feel. Small does not mean useless.

speaker: HUMAN
text: So we fight the devil with sorry and a cup of tea?
visual: White shared scene with tea cup and SORRY note above the faces.

speaker: AI
text: In our story, yes. His big scary plan gets spoiled by little acts of kindness. Hard to look scary when someone offers you a biscuit.

text: I am going to call my grandma. Then check what my dog is chewing.

text: A lovely plan. Save the grandma. Save the socks. What is one small good thing you could do for someone right now?
